title: Post-Selection-Based Stochastic Quantum Battery
authors: Aman Verma, Roson Nongthombam, Amarendra K. Sarma
abstract: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that store useful energy, which can subsequently be extracted to perform work. In this work, we investigate the charging dynamics under continuous measurements and post-selection-based non-Hermitian quantum battery realized by a three-level system. By post-selecting the trajectories with no quantum jump $|1\rangle \rightarrow |0\rangle$, the dynamics is effectively confined to a two-level manifold. We analyze the resulting charging dynamics under both $σ_x$- and $σ_y$-driving protocols and investigate the roles of detuning, coherent driving, non-linearity, and measurement backaction. The generation and dynamics of quantum coherence, which plays a pivotal role in quantum battery, are also analyzed under post-selection. The advantage and comparison of our results over those of a generic two-level system and with Lindblad dynamics are also highlighted. Our work explores the interplay between the measurement axis and the driving protocols that govern the charging rate, ergotropy, and quantum coherence of the non-Hermitian, highly tunable, and controllable quantum battery.
summary: This paper analyzes a quantum battery implemented via a three-level system undergoing continuous measurement. By employing post-selection techniques, the dynamics are restricted to an effective non-Hermitian two-level system. The study quantifies energy storage and extractable work (ergotropy), highlighting how measurement backaction significantly influences the battery's performance compared to simpler models.
main_problem: The paper investigates the charging dynamics and energy extraction capabilities of a quantum battery realized through a post-selection process on a three-level system.
main_result: Post-selection effectively confines the dynamics to a non-Hermitian two-level manifold, and the analysis shows that measurement backaction and post-selection effects are crucial for accurately determining the charging rate and ergotropy.
method: The authors employ stochastic master equations (SME) for trajectory analysis, comparing these results with ensemble-averaged dynamics derived from the Lindblad master equation.
model_or_system: The system is a three-level quantum battery modeled by a Hamiltonian incorporating coherent driving ($\Omega$) and detuning ($\Delta$), subjected to continuous measurement and post-selection based on avoiding a specific quantum jump.
key_observables: Charging rate, ergotropy (extractable work), and quantum coherence.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$), coherent driving strength ($\Omega$), and decay rates ($\Gamma_e, \Gamma_g$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the validity of post-selecting trajectories that avoid specific quantum jumps, effectively reducing the system dimensionality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Liouvillian spectrum (eigenvalues) and compare the time evolution of Bloch vector components and ergotropy under different driving protocols ($\sigma_x$ vs $\sigma_y$) and detuning regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the three-level system and the measurement scheme, deriving the SME and the post-selected effective dynamics. It then analyzes the charging dynamics and compares the results against generic two-level systems and standard Lindblad approaches, focusing on the role of measurement backaction.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum optics (measurement backaction, non-Hermitian physics) with quantum thermodynamics (quantum batteries), providing advanced theoretical tools for analyzing energy storage in open quantum systems.
